turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I keep losing a lot of time re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders, and going over conversations in my head. Especially before I leave the house or start work—I feel like I have to make sure I didn’t make some serious mistake.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes repetitive re-reading, reopening folders, and mentally replaying conversations to obtain reassurance that they have not made a serious mistake.

turns.doctor_question: When you re-read emails or go over conversations, do you feel like you're doing it to get rid of an unwanted, intrusive worry or fear—like something bad will happen if you don't—even though part of you knows it's excessive?
turns.patient_response: Yes. I keep going back over the emails, texts, folders, and conversations because I’m trying to make sure I didn’t make some serious mistake. I know I’m checking more than I need to, but I can’t really let it go until I’ve gone through it again.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes repetitive checking and mental reviewing to relieve fear of having made a serious mistake, recognizes it is excessive, and feels unable to stop until repeating it.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel the urge to re-check things, does it feel like an unwelcome intrusion that you wish would just go away, or does it feel more like it's just how you naturally are—careful, thorough, and wanting things done right?
turns.patient_response: It feels unwelcome. I’ll be trying to focus on a system design or prepare a lesson, and this thought barges in that maybe I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, mishandled family photos, or let someone in the community down. I know I’ve already gone over it, but I can’t seem to let it pass.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes recurrent, unwelcome thoughts that intrude while trying to focus and cannot be dismissed despite having already reviewed the concerns.

turns.doctor_question: When you go back and re-check the emails or conversations, does doing so give you at least some temporary relief or reduction in that anxious feeling, even if it comes back later?
turns.patient_response: Yes. Once I go through it again, I feel calmer for a little while—like I’ve finally made sure I didn’t miss something. But then later the doubt comes back, and I can lose a lot of time re-reading emails or replaying the conversation again.

symptom_reasoning.S066: Re-checking emails and mentally replaying conversations temporarily relieves anxiety, but the doubt returns and drives repetitive checking.
